Surah "Al-Sharh" (The Expansion)

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ He asked about the absence of expansion in the manner of denial, so it conveyed the affirmation of expansion. It is as if it were said: "We have expanded your breast for you." Therefore He conjoined to it: "and We removed," taking the meaning into account. That is: We made it spacious, with the knowledge and wisdom We deposited in it, until it encompassed the concerns of prophethood and the call of the two weighty things (mankind and jinn), and We removed from it the constriction and the distress that accompany blindness and ignorance. And from al-Hasan: "It was filled with wisdom and knowledge."

We relieved you of your burden (﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾), and We lightened for you the weights of prophethood and of undertaking its affair. It was said: it is a slip that is not recognized by its essence, namely leaving the better course while performing the good one, and prophets are reproved for the like of it. Its removal from him is that He forgave him. The word "al-wizr" (wizr): the heavy load.

"Which had weighed down your back" — that is, it made it heavy, until its creaking was heard, and that is the sound of breaking/cracking under strain (al-intiqad).

Note on rendering: the verse in the commentary is quoted as ﴿الَّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ﴾, so the translation of the Qur'anic words is:

﴿Which weighed down your back﴾

﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾. The raising of his remembrance is that his name is joined with the name of God in the *kalimat al-shahada* (the declaration of faith), the *adhan* (call to prayer), the *iqama* (the second call to prayer that immediately precedes the prayer), the *khutab* (sermons), and the *tashahhud* (the testimony recited in the prayer), and in more than one place in the Qur'an: ﴿Obey God and obey the Messenger﴾ [al-Nur: 54], ﴿And whoever obeys God and His Messenger﴾ [al-Nur: 52], (p-657) ﴿And God and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾ [al-Tawba: 62]. It is also seen in calling him "Messenger of God" and "Prophet of God," and in his being mentioned in the books of the earlier people.

The benefit of "for you" (*laka*) is what is known in the method of *ibham* (deliberate vagueness, leaving something unspecified at first) and *idah* (clarification). This is because it is understood from His words "Did We not expand for you" that there is something expanded, and then it was clarified by His words "your breast," which made known what had been vague. Likewise with "for you your remembrance" and "removed from you your burden."

﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾ ﴿Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾. That is, indeed with the hardship you are in, from enduring the affliction of the polytheists, there is ease through My making you victorious over them, until you overcome them. It is also said: the polytheists used to reproach the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers for their poverty, until it occurred to him that they had turned away from Islam because its adherents were poor. So He reminded him of the great blessings He had bestowed upon him, then said: ﴿Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾, as if He said: "We have granted you what We have granted you, so do not despair of the bounty of Allah, for indeed with the hardship you are in there is ease." The word "with" (*ma'a*) was used to indicate the closeness of ease to hardship, as an increase in consolation and a strengthening of hearts. When the verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Hardship will never overcome two eases," because the word "hardship" (*'usr*) is repeated in a definite form, so it is one thing; for when a definite noun is repeated in definite form, the second is the same as the first. The word "ease" (*yusr*) is repeated in an indefinite form, and when an indefinite noun is repeated in indefinite form, the second is different from the first. Thus the meaning becomes: "Indeed, with hardship there are two eases." Abu Mu'adh said: It is said, "Indeed, with the amir (commander) is a boy (*ghulaman*), indeed with the amir is a boy," so the amir is one and there are two boys with him. But if one says, "Indeed, with an amir is a boy, and indeed with the amir is the boy," then the amir is one and the boy is one. And if it is said, "Indeed, with an amir is a boy, and indeed with an amir is a boy," then they are two amirs and two boys. Thus it is in *Sharh al-Ta'wilat* (*The Explanation of the Interpretations*, a commentary on al-Nasafi's work).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 94, verse 7:

﴿So when you are free, then strive hard﴾. That is: when you are free from calling the creation (to God), then exert yourself in the worship of the Lord. And it is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with him and his father: "So when you are free from your prayer, then exert yourself in supplication." It is disputed whether this is before the salam (the closing greeting of the prayer) or after it. The connection with what precedes it is that when He enumerated His past blessings and His future promises to him, He prompted him to give thanks (shukr) and to exert himself in worship and in toil (naṣab) within it, and to link one act of worship with another, not leaving any of his times free of them. So when he finishes one act of worship, he follows it with another.
﴿And to your Lord direct your longing﴾. Make your desire directed to Him alone, and ask of none but His bounty, relying upon Him.
